one_line: Sonnet 5 review: strong benchmarks, but it uses so many tokens that cost per task exceeds Opus 4.8 despite a lower list price. Also covers Fable 5's return and Claude Code date-string fingerprinting.
summary: The host reviews Claude Sonnet 5, the first Sonnet update in about four and a half months, which Anthropic positions as its most agentic Sonnet with performance near Opus 4.8 at lower prices. He leans on Artificial Analysis rather than Anthropic's own benchmarks: Sonnet 5 is a few points behind Opus on the coding index, slightly ahead of GPT 5.4, and ahead of GPT 5.5 on the agentic index. The main argument is economic. A promotional price of $2/$10 per million input/output tokens lasts until August 31, then reverts to $3/$15. Sonnet 5 is very token-hungry (about 69,000 tokens per task on the Intelligence Index), so Artificial Analysis found its cost per task above Opus 4.8, and its full test-suite run cost more than Fable 5, though they used standard rather than discounted pricing. The host then covers Fable 5's return after export controls were lifted, with a limited window inside plan limits before usage-credit-only access, and the safeguard ban that followed a reported Amazon-researcher jailbreak. He notes other models reproduced the same vulnerability findings and exploit demos. Last, he describes a Claude Code change, reported in a third-party blog post, that alters the date string based on a China timezone and on API hostnames containing certain lab names, and he asks for more transparency about it.

key_ideas.idea: Sonnet 5 is positioned as Anthropic's most agentic Sonnet, close to Opus 4.8 at lower prices, and it beats Sonnet 4.6 on Anthropic's benchmarks.
key_ideas.detail: The host says Anthropic's own benchmarks show it nearing Opus on Terminal Bench and Computer Use and slightly beating Opus on knowledge work. He prefers third-party results from Artificial Analysis.

key_ideas.idea: On Artificial Analysis, Sonnet 5 trails Opus slightly on the coding index, leads GPT 5.4 slightly, and beats GPT 5.5 on the agentic index.
key_ideas.detail: The host reads this as evidence that the agentic-capability work paid off, even though its Intelligence Index placement sits between GPT 5.5 and GPT 5.4.

key_ideas.idea: List price misleads because Sonnet 5 uses far more tokens per task.
key_ideas.detail: The host reports about 69,000 tokens to run one Intelligence Index task, more than Sonnet 4.6, Opus 4.8, Fable 5, and GPT 5.4/5.5. On the score-versus-cost quadrant it sits at the far end from the efficient corner.

key_ideas.idea: Cost per task, not per-token price, is the decision metric; Sonnet 5 costs more per task than Opus 4.8.
key_ideas.detail: Artificial Analysis found it more expensive per task than Opus 4.8, beaten only by Fable. Its full suite cost more than Fable 5. Those figures use standard pricing, not the August promotional discount, so the host expects the final verdict depends on whether Anthropic extends the discount.

key_ideas.idea: On Cursor Bench, effort tiers do not translate into better value: Sonnet 5 Max scores below Opus 4.8 Extra High while costing more.
key_ideas.detail: Sonnet 5 High costs about the same as Opus 4.8 for a similar result. The host's conclusion is that Sonnet 5 has no clear niche between Opus 4.8 for daily work and Fable for hard tasks.

key_ideas.idea: Fable 5 returned after export controls were lifted, but access inside plan limits was a short window, and it is usage-credit only after July 7.
key_ideas.detail: The host says the model is available regardless of citizenship. Plan-limit access lasted about a week, or at least 50% of plan limits, and afterwards it requires usage credits.

key_ideas.idea: The Fable ban followed a reported jailbreak, but the host argues it did not prevent the capability: other models matched the vulnerability finding and exploit demo.
key_ideas.detail: According to the host's account of Anthropic's findings, Opus 4.8, GPT 5.5, Kimi K2.7 and several older Claude models identified the same vulnerability. Every model tested could demonstrate exploiting it. The host argues the main effect was stricter safeguards that block more routine requests, and that Fable is now falling back to Opus 4.8 more often, which he says affects benchmarks.

key_ideas.idea: Claude Code reportedly changes its system prompt's date string as a fingerprinting mechanism.
key_ideas.detail: According to a blog post the host cites, a China-timezone check switches the date separators from hyphens to slashes. If the API URL matches a list or the hostname contains keywords like DeepSeek, MiniMax or ZAI, the apostrophe in 'today's' is swapped for a visually identical Unicode character. The stated purpose is to detect API resellers, unauthorized gateways and distillation. The host calls it steganography and wants Anthropic to be more open about it.

techniques.name: Compare models by cost per completed task, not list price
techniques.how: Run a fixed task suite on each candidate model, record total input and output tokens plus spend per task, and compare score against cost per task (as Artificial Analysis does). Use the standard price, not a temporary discount, to see the steady-state cost.
techniques.when: Choosing a default model for an agent or routing layer, especially when a newer model is cheaper per token but may be more verbose.

techniques.name: Check the pricing basis of any cost comparison
techniques.how: Before trusting a cost comparison, confirm whether it uses standard or promotional pricing and whether it counts tokens or only per-token rates. The host flags that Artificial Analysis used standard prices, so a promotional discount would change the result.
techniques.when: Reading vendor or third-party cost claims, or setting budgets for a model that has a limited-time discount.

techniques.name: Compare effort tiers on the same benchmark
techniques.how: Test the same model at several effort levels (High, Max) and against a larger model at its top tier (Opus Extra High), and compare score and cost together. Look for cases where a cheaper model at high effort matches a pricier model at lower effort, or where the higher tier costs more without a better score.
techniques.when: Deciding which effort level or model tier to use for a task class, such as daily coding versus hard tasks.

tools: GPT 5.6 Terra (named; the host says he has no access)
Artificial Analysis (Coding, Intelligence and Agentic indices; quadrant chart)

numbers.claim: Sonnet 5 is the first Sonnet update in about four and a half months.
Promotional API price of $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens until August 31, then $3 and $15 (the standard Sonnet price).
About 69,000 tokens to run one task on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, more than Sonnet 4.6, Opus 4.8, Fable 5, GPT 5.4 and GPT 5.5.
Sonnet 5 cost more per task than Opus 4.8 on Artificial Analysis (only Fable was more expensive), and its full test suite cost more than Fable 5. Standard pricing was used.
GPT 5.5 is about half the price of Sonnet 5, and the host says it does better on most benchmarks (his claim).
Fable 5 plan-limit access lasted about a week (or at least 50% of plan limits) before usage-credit-only access after July 7.
Claude Code date-string change is triggered by a China-timezone check and by API hostnames matching a list or containing DeepSeek, MiniMax or ZAI.

hot_takes: Sonnet 5 is cheaper by list price but not by cost per task. The host says that cost is what matters, and that Opus 4.8 is the better daily driver for now.
The host says the Fable 5 jailbreak ban accomplished little because other models could reproduce the same vulnerability finding and exploit demo, and that it mainly blocks normal requests.
The host says Anthropic should be more honest about the Claude Code fingerprinting, even if he understands the anti-reseller and anti-distillation aim.
The host speculates that Anthropic might extend the discount or keep the lower price, which would change the comparison. This is speculation, not an announced change.

relevance.why: AgentOS strategy routing and budgets (Govrix Scout) depend on how much a model costs per task. This talk shows that per-token price can rank models differently from cost per completed task.
relevance.action: Make the routing and budget logic in Govrix Scout optimize on measured cost per completed task (tokens times price, averaged over a fixed task suite), not on list price per token, and re-run the comparison when a promotional price ends.

relevance.why: ProsHarness wraps the Claude Code CLI. The host reports that Claude Code may change system-prompt text based on the environment, which could affect a harness that depends on exact prompt content.
relevance.action: Verify that ProsHarness does not depend on exact Claude Code system-prompt text, such as the date line, and record the Claude Code version in each run so behavior changes can be traced.
